summary: Palatine farmer from Jettenbach who crossed on the Phoenix in 1754 and settled beside the Delaware just north of Easton; John's 6th-great-grandfather.
bio:
Johann Andreas Grub was born on 12 September 1727 at Jettenbach in the Duchy of Palatinate-Zweibrücken, in the Kusel district, the son of Johann Nickel Grub and Elisabeth Margaretha Lampert, and was baptized on the 21st of the month in the Lutheran parish of Reichenbach; his godparents included Maria Catharina, wife of Peter Grub, and Maria Elisabetha, wife of Adam Wendel. The baptism register fixes the date, and the 12 December on his gravestone is presumably a misreading. He married Maria Elisabetha Christmann at Jettenbach on 19 September 1752.

He was probably the "Anderas Groh" who landed at Philadelphia on the ship Phoenix on 1 October 1754; his presumed brother Johann Peter Grub (1724–1802) had come on the Windsor the year before. In Pennsylvania he belonged to the Williams Township congregation in 1759, was on the Bethlehem Township tax list in 1772 and at St. John's Lutheran Church in Easton in 1773, and had settled in Forks Township by 1781, where he held 100 acres in 1788. His tract adjoined the Delaware just north of colonial Easton, near the present campus of Lafayette College. An "Andrew Grub" of the Northampton County militia received a Militia Loan certificate during the Revolution, but that is not proof of service and may concern another man. Nor should he be confused with an earlier Andreas Grub whose wife Catharina had daughters baptized in Williams Township between 1748 and 1751, before this Andreas arrived.

His will, made on 11 November 1791, named his wife Mary Elizabeth and his children Philip, Catherine (who married Gottlieb Hipp), Mary (who married George Stacher), Elizabeth (who married Peter Michael), John, Frederick and Andrew, with the widow and Frederick as executors. He died in Forks Township on 6 August 1792 and was buried at St. John's Lutheran Cemetery, Easton. He was John's 6th-great-grandfather.

researchNotes:
Johann Andreas Grub was born at Jettenbach in the Duchy of Palatinate-Zweibrücken (Kusel district) in 1727, son of Johann Nickel Grub and Elisabeth Margaretha Lampert; WikiTree gives born 12 Sep, baptized 21 Sep 1727 (FamilySearch QPKL-RZNB, Reichenbach parish), his gravestone reads 12 Dec 1727, and GEDBAS gives 12 Jul 1727 (conflict; the tree shows 1727-1792). WikiTree flags a cousin of the same name as a possible confusion. He married Maria Elisabetha Christmann at Jettenbach on 19 Sep 1752. He was probably the 'Anderas Groh / Andreas Grub' on the ship Phoenix at Philadelphia, 1 Oct 1754 (Strassburger List 222); a 'Johannes Young/Jung' heads the same list. He appears in the Williams Twp congregation (1759), Bethlehem Twp tax list (1772), St. John's Lutheran, Easton (1773), and Forks Twp by 1781, with 100 acres in 1788; his tract adjoined the Delaware just north of colonial Easton, near today's Lafayette College campus. He died in Forks Twp on 6 Aug 1792 and was buried at St. John's Lutheran Cemetery, Easton (Find a Grave 28284890). His will of 11 Nov 1791 (Northampton Co. Register of Wills file #1430) names wife Mary Elizabeth and children Philip; Catherine (m. Gottlieb Hipp); Mary (m. George Stacher); Elizabeth (m. Peter Michael); John; Frederick; and Andrew; the widow and son Frederick were executors. An 'Andrew Grub' of the Northampton militia received a Militia Loan debt certificate (#10,758) - not proof of service and possibly another man (speculative). No French and Indian War service was found. A different 'Andreas Grub and w. Catharina' baptized daughters in Williams Twp 1748-1751, before this Andreas arrived - a separate man not to be merged. His presumed brother Johann Peter Grub (1724-1802) came on the Windsor in 1753. The tree profile shows a sailing-ship image.

The original Reichenbach Lutheran baptism register (page 93, year 1727), attached as an image to his FamilySearch profile, settles the birth date: under 'd. 12t 7br' [12 September] it records that Nickel Grub and his wife of Jettenbach had a son born, baptized on the 21st of the same month and named Joh. Andreas ([R4-S1]). The godparents included Maria Catharina, wife of Peter Grub, and Maria Elisabetha, wife of Adam Wendel. This confirms the 12 September date given by WikiTree and FamilySearch and rules out the 12 July of the GEDBAS database; the 12 December on his gravestone is presumably a misreading of '7ber' or '12br'.
